recipes.name: ui-flat-shape
recipes.parent: M_UI_Shape_Rectangle (Epic's UI shape material; check the exact name in the project)
recipes.use: Flat UI fill: rectangle with optional border and gradient, with interaction-state looks
steps: Create a material instance of the UI shape parent
Set fill on (1.0) or off (0.0)
Set stroke thickness and transparency
Switch gradient on for fill and/or stroke and set the colors with the boolean toggles
Set the state properties for hover, focus, press, disabled if the widget needs them
Assign a physical material (typically Wood) to avoid transparent edges
Drag the instance into the widget blueprint; combine several instances for a full design

recipes.name: barrier-texture-color-variants
recipes.use: Generic layout and naming for a Barrier material pack (parameter names differ per master, see the per-effect recipes barrier-hex-*, barrier-plasma-*, barrier-laser-*, barrier-shieldbubble-*)
steps: Folders: <Pack>/<Effect>/Material, MaterialInstance[/<Texture>], Texture, MaterialFunction
Names: MI_<Texture>_<Variant>_<NN>_<Color>, NN 00-09, rainbow Red Orange Yellow Green Mint Cyan Azure Blue Violet Magenta; hue-stepped sets use _H<degrees>
Always read the master's parameters with MaterialInstanceTools.list_parameters first: the names are NOT shared between masters
Create each instance with MaterialInstanceTools.create(folder_path, asset_name, parent) inside one execute_tool_script loop (never one MCP call per instance)
Recompile the master after any change, then save assets
Check every Barrier in the level uses its own instance and barrierDepth 0.01
Showcase: one wall per texture, 20 Barrier devices (10 Clear then 10 Dual), see barrier-showcase-layout

recipes.name: barrier-hex-texture-color-variants
recipes.use: Hex/Diamond/Triangle line textures in 10 rainbow colors, Clear (static lines on dark bar) and Dual (animated plasma underlay in the complementary color)
steps: Per texture set HexTexture (T_Hex_*, T_Diamond_*, T_Triangle_*) and LineColor = rainbow color
Clear: PlasmaAmount 0, BackgroundAmount 0, EmissiveIntensity 20, HexSpeedX 0.1, HexAngle 0, BackgroundColor (0.006,0.007,0.125)
Dual: PlasmaAmount 1, BackgroundAmount 1, EmissiveIntensity 2, HexSpeedX/Y about +-0.1, HexAngle/PlasmaAngle 0 or -45, PlasmaTexture T_Plasma_Checker, PlasmaTiling 2
Dual BackgroundColor (0.12 scale) and PlasmaColor (0.3 scale) use the COMPLEMENT of LineColor (cyan line -> red background; red line -> cyan 0,0.12,0.12 / 0,0.3,0.3)
Name MI_<Texture>_<Clear|Dual>_<NN>_<Color>, folder MaterialInstance/<Texture>
Create each instance with MaterialInstanceTools.create(folder_path, asset_name, parent) inside one execute_tool_script loop (never one MCP call per instance)
Recompile the master after any change, then save assets
Check every Barrier in the level uses its own instance and barrierDepth 0.01

recipes.name: barrier-plasma-texture-color-variants
recipes.use: Dissolve-pattern plasma barrier: 9 dissolve textures (+Shatter) x 10 rainbow colors
steps: Barrier Pattern = T_Shatter_Particles, Barrier Pattern UVs (5,3,0,0.091), Direction (0,1,0,0)
Dissolve Pattern1 = T_Plasma_Triangles and Dissolve Pattern2 = T_Plasma_Cells for Shatter; other sets swap these two for T_Plasma_Blocks/Checker/Circles/HexLines/HexThick/Squares/Stripes
Barrier Color = rainbow color (the only value that changes between the 10 instances)

Defaults used: Barrier Opacity 0.8, Position Mask Radius 300, Hardness 0.8, Final Pattern Contrast 10, Dissolve Glow Intensity 100, Border Opacity 0.1, Scale Min 1.5, Scale Max 2, Pattern Rotation Speed 0.05
Static switches Use Second Pattern, Enable Pattern Rotation, Enable Dynamic Scale all true (changing one recompiles shaders)
Name MI_Plasma_<Texture>_<NN>_<Color>, all in Plasma/MaterialInstance
Create each instance with MaterialInstanceTools.create(folder_path, asset_name, parent) inside one execute_tool_script loop (never one MCP call per instance)
Recompile the master after any change, then save assets
Check every Barrier in the level uses its own instance and barrierDepth 0.01

recipes.name: barrier-laser-line-variants
recipes.use: Scrolling laser lines: Filled and Lines in 10 colors, 20 tilt angles, 20 hue-stepped free variations
steps: Lines: Line Width 0.05, Emissive Intensity 100, Speed 0.5, Background Opacity 0.033, Tiling 1, Lines Color = rainbow, Background Color = darker shade of the same color (red: 0.8,0,0)
Filled: same as Lines but Background Opacity 0.55 and Background Color a light tint (red: 1,0.15,0.15)
Tilt (20, _00_000 to _19_090): Angle 0..90 in 20 steps (5th is 23.684), Line Width 0.1, Speed 0.6, Tiling 3, Background Opacity 0.03, Lines Color hue by index, Background Color (0.09,0.09,0.9)
Var (20, _H009 to _H351 step 18 degrees): Line Width 0.1, Speed and Speed X vary (-0.4,-0.3), Angle e.g. -45, Tiling about 5, Background Opacity 0.15
Name MI_Laser_<Filled|Lines>_<NN>_<Color>, MI_Laser_Tilt_<NN>_<angle>, MI_Laser_Var_<NN>_H<hue>
Create each instance with MaterialInstanceTools.create(folder_path, asset_name, parent) inside one execute_tool_script loop (never one MCP call per instance)
Recompile the master after any change, then save assets
Check every Barrier in the level uses its own instance and barrierDepth 0.01

recipes.name: barrier-shieldbubble-noise-variants
recipes.use: Intersecting shield bubble with caustics: one noise texture x a color set, in Rainbow and Dual folders
steps: Set MaskTexture and MaskTexture2 to a noise texture (T_CloudNoise, T_Noise_*, Mash_Noise, ShieldBubbleNoise2_M ...)

Color1 and Color_Caustics_A set the first hue, Color1_B and Color_Caustics_B the second (Dual); example hue H016: Color1 (1,0.267,0), Caustics_A (0,0.6,0.46), Caustics_B (1,0.56,0.4), Color1_B (0,1.5,1.15)
Per-texture tuning values to keep: WorldSpaceSize about 700, Distance Divisor 3000, IntersectingEdgeDivisor about 81, Fresnel_Pow about 2.7, Caustitcs_Brightness2 8, EdgeBrightness2 about 25
Folders: AllTextures_Rainbow (hue sweep), AllTextures_Dual (two-hue), ShieldBubbleNoise2 (20)
Name MI_<Noise>_<Rainbow|Dual>_H<hue>, hue in degrees
Create each instance with MaterialInstanceTools.create(folder_path, asset_name, parent) inside one execute_tool_script loop (never one MCP call per instance)
Recompile the master after any change, then save assets
Check every Barrier in the level uses its own instance and barrierDepth 0.01

recipes.name: rotating-rays-background
recipes.parent: Rotating background master material with an Img texture parameter
recipes.use: Rotating rays/glint background for UI widgets, with a rainbow variant
steps: Create the material instance and set_parent to the master material (instance and parent refPaths)
set_properties with TextureParameterValues: parameter Img, association GlobalParameter, index -1, value = ray texture refPath
Create a second instance for the rainbow variant with the same Img
Texture imports: set NeverStream false, rename with T_ prefix via move
save_assets, then delete old names
